offered_action_specs.name: rollback_deploy
offered_action_specs.description: Roll one service back to the settings it ran before its latest deploy, as the deploy log records them. Code plans it from that log, not from your tools' results, so you can name it even when they cannot see deploys: if the log holds no deploy of that service to undo, or the service changed since, code refuses it. Its container is recreated, so the service pauses while it restarts. Money already booked wrong stays wrong: a rollback stops new damage, and repairs nothing.

Successful 200s fell to zero by 16:48:43.

Each POST /payments that reaches the provider waits ~3 s and then fails with a 5xx. Some requests made more than one attempt and took ~6.2 s. That drives p95 latency to ~4.2 s.

The circuit breaker (PROVIDER_BREAKER=on) then opened. Most requests now fail fast with 503: 'circuit breaker is open', and the payment is left pending. Together these give the ~96% 5xx rate.

evidence.shows: payments-api ERRORs: 'provider unavailable; payment left pending'. The circuit breaker is open or half-open, after earlier attempts that failed with ReadTimeout.
From 16:47:58, ReadTimeout/no_answer attempts rose to ~1.4–1.6/s on /v1/payments and ~0.2/s on /v1/refunds. Over the same period, 200 answers fell from ~3/s to 0 by 16:48:43.

A POST /payments trace returned 503 after 3015 ms. Almost all of that time was one POST to fake-provider:8000/v1/payments that failed after 3009 ms with httpx.ReadTimeout. The Redis and Postgres spans were sub-millisecond.
Slow POST /payments and refund traces took ~3.0 s and ~6.2 s. These match one or two provider read timeouts per request.
The client latency histogram stays at ms levels. This fits timed-out calls not being recorded there, so it does not contradict the timeouts.
Every service, including payments-api, was created once at 16:46:16 with expected settings (PROVIDER_BREAKER=on, CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=cents). No change of ours lines up with the 16:48 onset.
All containers are running and healthy with 0 restarts, including fake-provider. The provider's process is up but not answering requests in time.

proposed_fix.summary:
No change on our side. The cause is the provider not answering in time.
1. Escalate to the provider (or investigate fake-provider) and check its status.
2. Keep the circuit breaker on. It sheds load and keeps POST /payments failing fast instead of hanging.
3. When the provider recovers, reconcile the payments left pending. Run money_check(wait=true) to find any calls that timed out on our side but were processed by the provider. Then confirm those through webhooks, or retry them idempotently with their existing keys.

diagnosis.blast_radius: Taking no action leaves payments and refunds failing, or left pending, until the provider recovers. Pending payments may diverge from the provider's records if timed-out calls were actually processed. A rollback or restart of our services would cause extra downtime and would not fix anything.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Nothing to undo, since no change is proposed. If a later mitigation is tried, such as changing the timeout or breaker settings, revert it to the settings recorded in the deploy log for 16:46:16.
